title: In-situ Spectroscopy and Post-Corrosion Electron Microscopy Study of Pure Vanadium in Molten Chloride Salt
content: Molten halide salts have gained significant attention in both advanced fission and fusion reactor concepts for their high-temperature heat transfer capabilities [1-2]. These are most prominently featured in novel molten salt reactor (MSR) designs as well as the affordable-robust-compact (ARC) tokamak reactor. Such salts are also favored for their thermal energy storage properties, heat conductivity, solubility for fissile materials, tritium breeding, and reduced activation effects. However, given the harsh reactor operating conditions, thorough re-examination of candidate structural alloys becomes essential. To this end, vanadium alloys rise to the challenge as promising candidate materials due to their excellent high-temperature strength, and outstanding radiation resistance [3-4]. Nevertheless, the application of vanadium as the primary constituent element in structural alloys remains relatively novel. Consequently, there exists a significant gap in the understanding of its corrosion performance under extreme conditions.
